definition: A plant with large red or pink bracts surrounding small yellow flowers, traditionally associated with Christmas.
origin: Poinsettia is named after Joel Roberts Poinsett (1779–1851), the first United States Minister to Mexico, who while serving there in the 1820s became fascinated by the vivid red plant growing wild and sent cuttings back to his greenhouses in South Carolina. His skill as an amateur botanist, alongside his diplomatic career, spread the plant through the United States, where it became a fixture of Christmas decoration.

definition: A sweet, orange-fleshed variety of melon with a rough, netted rind.
origin: Cantaloupe takes its name from Cantalupo, a former papal estate near Rome where the melon was reportedly cultivated after seeds arrived from Armenia in the fifteenth century, though some scholars trace the name instead to a town of the same name in southern France. Either way, the fruit carried an Italian place name into English, even as European and American varieties later diverged.

definition: A salad of chopped apples, celery, walnuts, and grapes bound in mayonnaise.
origin: Waldorf salad is named after the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel in New York City, where maître d'hôtel Oscar Tschirky created it around 1893, reportedly for the hotel's opening. His original version contained just apples, celery, and mayonnaise, with walnuts added to the recipe only later, but the hotel's name has stayed attached to the dish through every variation since.

definition: A salad of chopped lettuce, tomato, bacon, chicken, hard-boiled egg, avocado, and blue cheese, arranged in rows.
origin: Cobb salad is named after Robert Cobb (1899–1970), owner of the Hollywood Brown Derby restaurant, who is said to have thrown the dish together in 1937 from leftovers in his kitchen late one night to feed himself and a hungry visiting friend. The improvised combination proved so popular with regulars that it became a permanent, and now iconic, fixture of the menu.

definition: A drink or flavour combining coffee and chocolate.
origin: Mocha takes its name from Mocha, a port city in Yemen that from the fifteenth to the seventeenth centuries was the world's principal hub for coffee export, giving its name simply to coffee itself for a time. The specific coffee-chocolate flavour pairing came later, but it kept the port city's name attached, long after Mocha's trading importance had faded.

definition: A thick, boneless cut of beef steak, typically from the rib section, known for its rich marbling.
origin: Delmonico steak takes its name from Delmonico's, the restaurant opened in New York City in 1837 by Swiss brothers John and Peter Delmonico, widely credited as America's first fine-dining establishment. The restaurant served a particular well-marbled cut of steak that became so associated with its name that "Delmonico" is still used for that style of steak today, long after the original restaurant closed.

definition: A tart, crisp, bright green variety of apple, formally called the Granny Smith.
origin: Granny Smith apples are named after Maria Ann "Granny" Smith (1799–1870), an English-born orchardist in New South Wales, Australia, who around 1868 discovered a chance seedling growing from discarded French crab apples near a creek on her property. She propagated the tart, green apple herself, and it became one of the most widely grown apple varieties in the world, still carrying her homely nickname.
